identity.name: Trishakti Industries Limited
identity.industry: Infrastructure Services / Heavy-Lifting & Construction-Equipment Rental (crane hiring)

summary.oneLiner:
A ₹372cr-mcap, BSE-only crane-hiring company that was restructured into a single-business infrastructure
services play after an FY24 family separation, and is now compounding off a very small base by buying
machines as fast as banks and cash flow allow. Q3 FY26 standalone revenue was **₹8 crores** (+20% QoQ,
+357% YoY) with 9M revenue ₹18.74cr — but the signal is the balance sheet, not the P&L: against a guided
FY26 capex of ₹100cr the company has **already deployed ₹154cr** of machines YTD and has spent ₹200cr of
a ₹400cr FY28 programme, with the fleet at **117 machines at 100% utilisation**. The revenue lags the
asset by a stated one-to-one-and-a-half-month mobilisation lead time, so the ₹200cr block only began
earning fully in Q3/January. The demand pull is renewables — **45% of the fleet is on renewable-energy
sites** (solar and BESS, explicitly *not* wind) — plus L&T's bullet-train project, metros and steel.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Positions itself as one of India's leading pure-play infrastructure equipment rental companies (crawler cranes, truck-mounted cranes, all-terrain cranes, piling rigs, manlifters up to 750MT), transformed since the 2023 promoter family separation from a diversified electronics/trading business.
- Structural moat from technical expertise, high entry barriers, and Tier-1 relationships with L&T, Adani, and Reliance, ensuring repeat business, pricing discipline, and long-term revenue visibility.
- Niche heavy-lift specialization (100-750T) creates pricing power - few operators can safely execute this segment, commanding premium rates and natural barriers to entry.
- Tier-1 client lock-in: once on an approved vendor list (e.g. Reliance, L&T), repeat work arrives without re-tendering; new vendor onboarding takes 6-12 months, making the relationship structurally sticky.
- Over 100 satisfied clients including L&T, Reliance, RVNL, ONGC, ITD Cementation, Adani Group, KEC Industries, Jindal Group, Tata Steel and NCC.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **One operating segment that matters: heavy equipment hiring.** Segment assets ₹200cr. Management
  instructed modelling off this line alone; "Others" (₹11.43cr segment assets, negative Q3 result) is the
  FOC/credit-note contra described in §2. From FY27 there will be a single reported stream.
- **No subsidiaries were named on the call**, despite the cover letter referring to consolidated results.
- **Geography:** *"We are available pan-India. We are working in almost, like, everywhere. In the East, we
  have lesser machines, except in Odisha."*
- **End-market mix:** renewables **45%** of exposure today — *"on the renewable energy side, if you see on
  a pie chart basis, right now, we are at 45% exposure to the renewable energy side… our asset base is
  around INR 200 crores. That is the reason why around INR 80 crores, INR 90 crores of the machines are
  into the renewable energy side."* Management expects the *share* to fall as the block grows: *"suppose
  on INR 400-crore block, if you got INR 120-crore machines, the sector, then it's just 30%."*
- **Client concentration is acknowledged and bounded to blue-chips:** *"maybe on a three-month basis or a
  six-month basis, maybe our order book can come from, like, 30% to 40% -- 40% of our order book can come
  from one company also… But in the longer term, maybe if you take a 12-month thing, then it will get
  blended again."*

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- **₹48cr** signed as at 31-Dec-2025 → **₹55–56cr** at the call date, on contracts won *"in the past two weeks."*
- **Contract tenor:** *"We get six months' orders to twelve months' orders"*, but *"whatever contracts we
  have recently entered, all are 12 months and above contracts."* Underwriting is done to project life,
  not contract life: *"before we actually take an order from a client, we have a full survey on the site
  where we make sure that the project should at least go on for the next two years or so."*
- **Longest-running deployment:** the first machine bought post-restructuring, placed with Jindal — *"it
  has been two years already. That machine is still running over there only."*
- **Order book is a rolling renewal book, not a backlog to burn:** *"as and when our contracts keep
  getting renewed, this ARR will also keep going up."* Churn illustration: *"if 250-ton machine contract
  is expiring in February, so technically speaking, I just have a 30-lakh contract left. But if it gets
  extended another 12 months, then I'm again good with INR 2-crore order."*
- **Phase visibility:** *"we have entered in the phase 1 of these particular projects, and there are still
  three more phases to go after this. So, we do see that there is good revenue visibility for the next two
  years or three years."*
- **Named clients:** *"marquee clients including Larsen and Toubro, Reliance, Jindal Group, KEC
  International and ITD Cementation anchoring our order book."* Plus a **bullet-train** deployment:
  *"Recently, we had won an order for the bullet train project as well. So, L&T is doing that project. So,
  we have given a few machines over there as well."*
- **Utilisation:** *"All the machines are at 100% utilization as of now. Our last set of machines, which
  will be 110-ton machines and the 150-ton machines have also been started around January 10. So right
  now, since we are talking, we are at full capacity right now."*

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **FY26 revenue:** prior guidance was **₹20–22 crores** (from the investor presentation, per the analyst
  question, not restated by management as a new number). Management guided to a **beat**: *"this financial
  year, if you've seen the first three quarters itself, we have done almost INR 19 crores of revenue, and
  our guided revenue was INR 20 to INR 22 crores. And now we are at peak capacity. So this year, we will
  be surpassing by a good percentage."*
- **Forward revenue on the existing book (calendar basis):** *"from December last year to December this
  financial year, we'll be talking INR 55 crores of revenue, even if you stop expanding right now."*
  Repeated: *"right now, with the stock expanding, we should be doing INR 55 crores of revenue for sure
  with our current order book."*
- **FY28 revenue target ₹100 crores:** management would **not** commit. Asked directly, the answer was
  *"We generally feel that there is a very high time because of the kind of demand we are seeing right
  now. But we don't want to commit to anything. But with our current order book, we are already 55%, 60%
  there, and it's literally two years."*
- **Margin:** EBITDA *"65% to 70% range"* while OEM free-maintenance runs; stepping down to *"around 60%
  to 65% EBITDA margins"* once maintenance kicks in after 3–4 years. **PAT margin 25–30%**: *"It will be
  anywhere between 25% to 30%… for the next three years, four years, this 25%, 30% margin should always
  be stabilized only."*
- **Capex:** ₹400cr programme through **FY28**; ₹200cr spent. FY26 target was ₹100cr, **₹154cr already
  deployed YTD** — *"our FY26 CapEx target was INR 100 crores and we are delighted to announce that we
  have already deployed INR 154 crores worth of machines year to date."* Management explicitly declined
  to raise the headline number when pushed: *"my target is that let's read the 400 number first… INR 400
  crore to INR 500 crore is a genuine number… In order to go to INR 1,000 crores, then we'll be needing
  further internal approvals."*
- **Reporting change:** single revenue-stream segment from **FY27** (see §2 one-offs).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Solar + BESS is the live driver:** *"in the last six months itself, we have seen that in the renewable
  energy segment, the demand is skyrocketing like anything. So be it in the solar part and the BESS plants
  as well. So recently, we have got a lot of orders related to the BESS industry battery storage."*
  Confirmed on follow-up: *"Yes. It's mainly solar and the battery storage."*
- **Metros are a pipeline, not yet revenue:** *"Even the metro side is growing really fast, but the
  projects are still yet to open. A few of the biggest EPC contractors have just won the orders, so it
  will take around two months to three more months for the civil work to be done. And then they'll get the
  crane and manufacture requirements. So, we are just waiting for those particular things."*
- **Reliance as a multi-vertical annuity:** *"Reliance getting into renewable energy has been a really
  good thing for us… it's not that reliance is only doing renewable energy. They have other things as
  well. They are into chemicals. Like, they are building India's biggest chemical vinyl plant as well…
  the machinery requirements are in all sectors, be it solar, be it renewable, be it metros, be it steel,
  anything."*
- **Higher-tonnage fleet is the stated next step:** *"we are focusing on expanding our next-generation
  higher tonnage fleet to support large scale industrial and renewable projects."*
- **Deliberately NOT wind** — see §10.
- **Fleet-churn arbitrage (management's own idea, not a committed plan):** *"every seven years, there is a
  spike in the metal prices… if you time your exit on those years, then you can get a good 10% extra
  premium for the machines because our machines are literally metal."*

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **EBITDA 65–70% now → 60–65% structurally** once OEM maintenance rolls off after year 3–4 (the "5% hit"
  peers already take).
- **Asset yields, stated monthly:** lower-tonnage (~100t) *"we can generate up to 3% or 2.8%, 3%… With
  over time, we can also go to 3.5% of net revenue"*; higher-tonnage (250t/500t) *"our net revenue will be
  2.5% only. But the operational cost in both machines will just be 0.2% or 0.3%. So, our net blended
  yield will be similar in both the cases."* Clarified as **monthly**, i.e. ~30–35% p.a. on asset value,
  with H2 overtime upside: *"in H2, we get a lot of overtimes… if our yields are 30% per annum, and in
  some years, we can generate 36% also."*
- **Payback:** *"an efficient payback cycle of around 3 years to 3.5 years for our equipment investments."*
- **Depreciation is the PAT-margin engine and the tax shield.** SLM, not WDV: *"we use the SLM method. We
  do not use the written down one. So in the income tax, we do get 15% depreciation benefit. And in the
  books, on 100 tons and above, we get 4.75% of depreciation. And on 100 tons and below, it's a 6.3%"*
  [transcript reads "appreciation" — evidently depreciation]. Life: *"on the income tax, we depreciate
  machines in seven years. But in the balance sheet, we depreciate machines about 22 years. It's around
  twenty years."*
- **GST input credit is a cash-flow, not P&L, item and management understands it as a treadmill:** *"if my
  payback cycle is supposed hypothetically four years, then after four years, I will be needing at least
  18% of my new CapEx to be done so that GST benefit comes in to me."* Also: *"if I'm doing INR 10 crore
  revenue, I'm actually getting paid INR 11.8 crores because GST is not shown in our revenue. But if you
  see, GST is being blocked."*
- **Revenue lag:** *"our lead time for the machines to start generating revenue is around one and a half
  months… it does take time for our machines to reach the site, get the TPI done, logbook started, diesel
  book started, so there are many compliances."* This is the stated reason Q3 grew only 20% QoQ vs 63% in
  Q2, and why *"whatever CapEx is being done in Q3, the real fruits we'll be getting within Q4."*

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **Funding stack:** 100% LTV asset finance plus equity. *"when we buy machines, we buy machines at a 100%
  LTV through either a three-year funding or a four-year funding. So, our repayments are also quite fast.
  And we have raised two equity rounds as well in the past one and a half years."*
- **Equity funded the first half of the programme:** *"although INR 200 crores of CapEx we have done, so
  as I had mentioned earlier that we have raised two rounds of equity, which has helped us to buy more and
  more machines and to mobilize the INR 200 crores worth of machines."* Neither round's size, price or
  dilution was disclosed on the call.
- **Second half is intended to be internally funded:** *"with this particular internal accruals on a
  monthly basis, whatever cash we have generated, we'll reinvest that cash into buying new machines. So
  this is how, organically, we are slowly and steadily growing our asset base."*
- **Almost no working-capital line:** *"We don't have any kind of working capital limit… We just have INR
  2 crore bank limit, like OD facility"* — against a ₹200cr asset base. Liquidity depends on blue-chip
  bill discounting (§6a) rather than a sanctioned limit.
- **OEM moratoriums bridge mobilisation:** *"we do get some small moratoriums from the OEMs as well for
  the smooth operation in part. So, it's not that we get such lucrative deals also, but… as soon as the
  machines have reached the site, we start repaying them in terms of long-term borrowings on it, which is
  the CVC funding for the banks."*
- **No dividend, buyback or debt-reduction discussion took place on this call.**

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body:
Confident, unusually candid, and commercially fluent — but thin on controls. Positives: the CEO refused
to raise the ₹400cr capex headline when an investor pushed him twice (*"investors like clarity… it's
always better to be practical… we don't want to overcommit anything"*), refused to commit to the FY28
₹100cr target, volunteered the family-separation history unprompted, and gave genuinely specific unit
economics (monthly yields by tonnage, mobilisation costs, depreciation rates under both books). He also
correctly and publicly steered analysts *away* from a flattering-looking segment line. Negatives: he could
not produce a 9M cash-flow figure, needed time to locate a segment-asset number an investor was reading
from the company's own filing, and the ARR/order-book figures collapse onto the same ₹48cr. Portions of
the Q&A were conducted in Hindi and are rendered as unreadable glyphs in the filed transcript's text
layer — the substance of those exchanges (FY27 ₹60–65cr revenue question, PAT-margin question, FY28
₹100cr question) is recoverable only from the English answers, which are quoted above.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position (OPTIONAL — evidenced on this call)
moat.body:
- **OEM free-maintenance window is the entire margin gap vs peers.** Asked directly why margins beat
  listed peers: *"the major part of that why we are clocking 70% EBITDA margin. The major, major reason is
  that, we don't have to pay for any maintenance for the first three years because it's covered by the
  OEMs of late. So, that is the reason why we don't take an additional 5% hit, which most of our
  competitors are taking."* **This is a young-fleet advantage with a stated expiry** — management itself
  guides margins down to 60–65% when maintenance starts. It is a timing moat, not a durable one.
- **De-hire economics create real switching friction.** *"the customer can de-hire our machines, but if
  they de-hire our machines, they have to give us a 30-day grace period. And post this grace period,
  they'll also have to pay for the one side of the mobilization of the machines."* Quantified:
  *"if I'm generating INR 15 lakhs of income on a monthly basis from a 260-ton machine… the mobilization
  cost on one side is around INR 20 lakhs, INR 25 lakhs. So, we'll be getting that as well. So, this is
  the major reason why, generally, nobody gets de-hired very easily until unless you're doing a bad job."*
- **Blue-chip-only counterparty policy = a financing moat, explicitly.** *"we have a business mantra that
  we do not work with the local subcontractors… if I'm working with companies like Tata, Jindal, Reliance
  and all, I can always get their bills discounted if I'm on any kind of cash crunch in the future… if we
  start working with the subcontractors, the local subcontractors, their payment will start hitting our
  accounts in next five months, six months."*
- **Incumbency predates the restructuring.** *"we are into this industry since 1997… we were always linked
  with L&T, Reliance. We were always their vendors. It's just that right now, everything is being
  restructured. That's why it's looking like we are newcomers in this industry, but it's not like that."*

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **9M operating cash flow was not disclosed** (§2). The self-funding claim is unverified from this call.
2. **Receivables are stretched** and the fix is a promise about future quarters, not an action taken.
3. **A ₹2cr OD facility against a ₹200cr asset base** leaves essentially no committed liquidity buffer if
   a large blue-chip client slows payment.
4. **Margin has a dated expiry.** The 65–70% EBITDA depends on OEM free maintenance for the first three
   years; management guides 60–65% after. As the fleet ages, this compresses mechanically.
5. **Concentration:** up to 40% of the order book from a single client over a 3–6 month window, and 45%
   of the fleet on renewable-energy sites — a single-sector capex pause would hit hard.
6. **Order book ≈ 3x quarterly revenue and is renewal-dependent**, not contracted backlog; the February
   250-ton example shows how fast the book can shrink if a renewal is missed.
7. **De-hire risk is mitigated but not eliminated** — the 30-day grace + mobilisation recovery is
   compensation, not prevention.
8. **Wind is a segment they have deliberately exited/avoided, on a regulatory change:** *"for wind energy,
   you need more than 750 ton-plus and 900 ton-plus machines… the government had also raised a new rule
   that the average height of the windmill has been like, suppose if it was 10 meters, then it has been
   moved to around 11 or 12 meters. So because of that, most of the 750-ton machines are now not usable
   for the wind energy segment. So, we did not take that hit."* Read this as a **live warning about
   technical obsolescence risk in this asset class** — a rule change stranded a peer's fleet.
9. **Percentage growth rates are base-effect artefacts** (+1,744% PAT YoY on ₹2.45cr).
10. **Governance/disclosure texture:** the MD who signed the filing was absent; the CEO answered a
    segment-asset question with *"Just a second… I'll have to check what you're exactly implementing to
    once"*; and only 7 participants (three of them individual investors) were on the call.
11. **Metro conversion is undated beyond "two to three months" of civil work** — watch whether crane
    requirements actually materialise.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The stock is a levered call on someone else's capex, one step removed.** Management says so plainly:
  *"we are secondary benefiters of this thing."* Cranes are mobilised *before* a plant produces anything,
  so this business turns up **early** in a capex cycle — and, by the same logic, will roll over early.
- **The reported revenue understates the installed earning power by roughly a quarter's lag.** ₹200cr of
  assets only reached full utilisation in January, while Q3 revenue was ₹8cr. The Q4 print, not Q3, is the
  first clean read on the deployed block.
- **Segment "Others" going negative is a *positive* signal misread as a loss** — it is FOC spares received
  free with machines being consumed. Two separate analysts read it as a loss on this call.
- **The single most quantitative disclosure was about a business they refuse to enter.** The wind-energy
  answer (750t machines stranded by a windmill-height rule) is the sharpest competitive intelligence on
  the call and it concerns a peer's problem, not theirs.
- **Depreciation policy is a deliberate optical choice:** SLM over ~20–22 years in the published books
  (flattering reported PAT) against 7 years / 15% for income tax (minimising cash tax). Both were
  volunteered openly.
- **The "order book" is a monthly-rental annuity dressed as a backlog.** ₹55–56cr is roughly 12 months of
  rentals on machines already on site, so it renews rather than depletes — which is why ARR and order book
  converge on the same number.

triggers.title: Near-term trigger — NONE CARRIED FORWARD (window lapsed)
triggers.body:
**No trigger is recorded for this note and all four `_agg` trigger fields are left empty**, per SPEC §10
(*"hard-dated, high-impact catalysts in the next ~3 months"*, assessed as of **today, 13-Aug-2026**).

The call was held **20-Jan-2026**. Every forward-dated item on it sat inside a window that has now
**fully lapsed** — roughly **Feb–Apr 2026**, some six to seven months ago:

- *"it will take around two months to three more months for the civil work to be done"* (metro crane
  requirements) → **~Mar–Apr 2026. LAPSED.**
- *"whatever CapEx is being done in Q3, the real fruits we'll be getting within Q4"* → **Q4 FY26
  (Jan–Mar 2026). LAPSED** — Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 have both since been reported.
- *"this year, we will be surpassing by a good percentage"* (FY26 revenue beat vs ₹20–22cr guidance) →
  **FY26 year-end, 31-Mar-2026. LAPSED.**
- *"if we are able to generate more demand before the upcoming monsoons"* / *"another INR 100 crores of
  CapEx… in the next 6 months only"* → **~Jul 2026. LAPSED.**
- Single-revenue-stream segment reporting **from FY27** → first FY27 reporting period has already passed.

The only genuinely still-forward items are the **₹400cr capex programme through FY28** and the **FY28
₹100cr revenue aspiration** — both are multi-year and explicitly *not* committed by management
(*"we don't want to commit to anything"*), so neither qualifies under SPEC §10's near-term, hard-dated,
verifiable test. These are **verification items for the next call**, not catalysts.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)
challenges.body:

> `output/concall/companies.csv` + `products.csv` and `shadow_paths.load_stock_metadata()` only —
> no web lookups. ✅ = already covered in our concall corpus · ⭐ = sector knowledge, code verified
> against the metadata frame. Where nothing resolves cleanly, the cell is left **unmapped** by design.

|---|---|---|---|
| *"in the renewable energy segment, the demand is skyrocketing like anything. So be it in the solar part and the BESS plants as well. So recently, we have got a lot of orders related to the BESS industry battery storage."* — a shortage of **lifting capacity at renewable construction sites** | **531279** (BSE-only, Heavy-Lifting & Construction-Equipment Rental) — Trishakti itself, the direct pricing-power holder at 100% utilisation ✅ | Solar/BESS EPC developers, who now bid for scarce high-tonnage cranes as an input cost | **High.** Directly evidenced: fleet at 100% utilisation, capex overshoot 154% of plan, and management's own *"secondary benefiters"* framing. The beneficiary here is the company on the call; peer crane-hirers are alluded to (*"one other competitor"*, *"one listed player"*) but **never named**, so no second name is mapped rather than guessing. |
| *"we don't have to pay for any maintenance for the first three years because it's covered by the OEMs of late. So, that is the reason why we don't take an additional 5% hit, which most of our competitors are taking."* — a **maintenance-cost asymmetry between young and old fleets** | **unmapped** — the crane OEMs absorbing the maintenance were not named on the call, and no listed Indian crane OEM resolves from `companies.csv` / `products.csv` | Incumbent crane-hire operators running out-of-warranty fleets — **unnamed by management** | **Med** on the mechanism, **unmappable** on the names. So because of that, most of the 750-ton machines are now not usable for the wind energy segment."* — a **regulatory stranding of 750t-class cranes** | **531279** (BSE-only) relatively, by non-participation: *"we did not take that hit because we were not in the wind energy segment"* ✅ | Crane-hire operators with 750t/900t fleets built for wind — **unnamed**; and by extension wind-turbine installers facing a tighter heavy-lift pool | **Med.** The rule change is stated as fact by management but not sourced or dated on the call, and no affected listed operator is named. Treat as an unverified second-hand regulatory claim until confirmed independently. |
| *"Reliance getting into renewable energy has been a really good thing for us… they are building India's biggest chemical vinyl plant as well"* — **client capex concentration in a few very large groups** | **RELIANCE** (532540 BSE · Oil-to-Chemicals & New Energy) named as *"one of our biggest… clients"*; **LT** (500510 BSE · Infrastructure EPC) named as the bullet-train contractor; **JINDALSTEL/Jindal Group** (532286 BSE · Steel), **KEC** (532714 BSE · T&D EPC), **ITDCEM** (509496 BSE · Infrastructure EPC) named as anchor clients ⭐ | Local/regional subcontractors, whom Trishakti refuses to serve: *"if we start working with the subcontractors, the local subcontractors, their payment will start hitting our accounts in next five months, six months"* | **High on the naming** (all five are verbatim from the opening remarks / Q&A), **Low as an investment read** — these are Trishakti's *customers*, so the read-through runs the other way: they are the source of its concentration risk, not beneficiaries of its call. A few of the biggest EPC contractors have just won the orders, so it will take around two months to three more months for the civil work to be done."* — **a demand pocket that has not converted yet** | **unmapped** — the "biggest EPC contractors" who won the metro orders were not named | Trishakti itself, near-term: capacity is committed while metro demand waits | **Low.** Explicitly forward-looking and undated beyond a 2–3 month civil-works estimate from 20-Jan-2026 — i.e. **already elapsed** as of 13-Aug-2026 with no confirmation available in this file. qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q3 FY26 (this — first note for this company):** Revenue ₹8cr (+357% YoY), 9M ₹18.74cr; EBITDA ₹5.61cr
  (9M margin 65.27%); PAT ₹2.45cr (9M ₹4.97cr). Capex over-run: ₹154cr deployed vs ₹100cr FY26 plan;
  ₹200cr of the ₹400cr FY28 programme done. Fleet 117 machines, 100% utilisation. Order book ₹48cr at
  31-Dec → ₹55–56cr at call date. Renewables 45% of fleet exposure (solar + BESS; **no wind**). 9M cash
  flow **not disclosed**. Two equity rounds raised in the prior ~18 months, sizes undisclosed.
- _Q4 FY26 → check: (a) did FY26 revenue beat the ₹20–22cr guidance and by how much; (b) **the 9M/FY26
  operating cash-flow number that was promised offline**; (c) whether receivables actually normalised;
  (d) FY26 exit capex vs the ₹400cr programme and whether the FY27 ₹100cr add-on happened before the

other.body:
- [Management Note] Q4FY26/FY26 Other Income includes ₹4.58 Cr of subvention income linked to equipment financing, which management considers operational in nature and part of the operating model despite its separate accounting classification.
- [Leadership Transition] Following the 2023 promoter family separation, a new leadership team (Dhruv Jhanwar - CEO, Pranav Jhanwar - CFO, Suresh Jhanwar - MD/Chairman) took charge and redefined the business from a diversified electronics/trading/financial-activities model into an asset-backed infrastructure equipment rental company.
- [Listing] Trishakti Industries is listed on BSE (Security Code 531279) and the Calcutta Stock Exchange (Scrip Code 10030166); ISIN INE238C01022.
